_comment: DISPATCH POLICY — you own this file. Claude reads it; Claude never writes it.
Every lane carries a `mode` of exactly one of three values:
auto    Claude may dispatch this lane without asking you first.
ask     Claude must get your explicit per-request approval in chat before dispatching.
reject  Never dispatch. The script refuses and says this config forbade it.
This file is the single source of truth for policy. Changing a mode changes
behaviour with no code edit. Writing `auto` here IS your standing approval for
that lane — the script does not second-guess it and does not downgrade it.
A lane you delete from `lanes` is not thereby allowed. An unlisted lane is
treated as `ask`, and the script says the config did not mention it. There is
no config switch that makes an unlisted lane `auto`.
An unrecognised mode value is also treated as `ask`, with a warning naming it.
WHAT THE SCRIPT ENFORCES REGARDLESS OF THIS FILE:
1. A lane whose availability probe does not come back READY is never
dispatched. Unknown is not the same as available.
2. `--dry-run` never executes anything, whatever the mode says.
3. A `-fast` Cursor slug is WARNED about, loudly, and then run anyway.
It is your allowance to spend.
4. A `trustFlag` value it does not recognise is REJECTED, not forwarded.
That string would become an argument to a CLI, so a typo here fails the
dispatch (exit 5) instead of being passed through.
5. Any `trustFlag` in force is named, with what it grants, in both the
`--dry-run` preview and the `ask` approval message — so you never approve
a dispatch without seeing the grant it carries.
COST AND RISK, PER LANE:
codex        HIGHEST RISK. Your ~/.codex/config.toml sets
sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access", so this lane runs with full
filesystem access and no approval prompts. It can delete or
rewrite anything this account can reach. Nothing in this repo
changes that config; only you should. Keep it `ask` unless you
have a specific reason not to.
deepseek     METERED. Costs real money per call, billed to OpenCode Go.
antigravity  Has a ~16k input-token floor per call. There is no cheap `agy`
call; a one-line question costs about what a long one does.
composer     Shares one Cursor allowance with `grok`.
grok         Shares one Cursor allowance with `composer`. Composer is the only
lane rated for long multi-file agentic runs, so Grok spending
comes directly out of a lane that has no substitute. Prefer Grok
for analysis and single-shot reasoning, and keep the budget for
Composer's long builds.
minimax      Included in the MiniMax coding plan: unlimited weekly, but a
limited rolling 5-hour window.
OPTIONAL PER-LANE KEYS:
model    Model slug for lanes that take one. Omit to use the value in
`defaults` below (shown by `node check_lanes.js`).
binary   Absolute path to the CLI, if it is not on PATH and not at the
known install location. Omit unless you have moved it.
note     Free text. The script echoes it; it has no effect on behaviour.
trustFlag
A STANDING PERMISSION granted to one lane. Omit it, or set it to
null, and no flag is passed at all. It exists because two of the
CLIs cannot prompt when run non-interactively and fail rather than
ask: cursor-agent refuses to start in an untrusted directory
("Workspace Trust Required"), and agy auto-DENIES any tool
permission it cannot prompt for, returning no work done.
THIS KEY GRANTS A PRIVILEGE. Delete it to revoke that grant; no code
change is needed, which is the whole reason it lives here.
THE ACCEPTED VALUES ARE PER-CLI, NOT GLOBAL. Each lane accepts only
the literals its own CLI understands. A value valid on another lane
is a HARD ERROR here, not something forwarded for the CLI to trip
over — "--yolo" on `antigravity` and
"--dangerously-skip-permissions" on `composer` both fail the
dispatch (exit 5) naming the set that lane does accept.
composer, grok  (cursor-agent) — read from `cursor-agent --help`
"--trust"  Trusts this directory, and nothing more. Every command
the agent wants to run is still approved individually.
This is the SMALLEST grant that fixes the trust error.
"--yolo"   Alias for `--force` — "Run Everything". AUTO-APPROVES
EVERY COMMAND THE AGENT RUNS, unless explicitly denied.
Materially larger than trusting the directory: the agent
executes shell commands with no per-command approval.
"-f"       The short form of `--force`. Same grant as `--yolo`.
antigravity     (agy) — read from `agy --help`, agy 1.1.20, on
"--dangerously-skip-permissions"
AUTO-APPROVES EVERY TOOL THE AGENT RUNS, without
prompting. This is a LARGER grant than trusting a
directory: it covers every tool permission request, not
just the workspace. agy offers NO smaller alternative —
there is no directory-trust-only flag to fall back to,
so this is the only value that clears the failure.
minimax, deepseek (opencode) and codex accept NOTHING here. Set on
one of those the value is IGNORED with a warning and never reaches
the command line; those CLIs would reject it as an unknown argument.
Any other value is a hard error; the dispatch refuses rather than
passing an unrecognised flag to a CLI.

minimax.note: Reviewing and verification, not implementation. Slow but more powerful. Runs on omp (Oh My Pi), NOT opencode, as of 2026-08-25 — the slug is the omp provider id `minimax-code`, and it must be an EXACT entry in `omp models --json` or the dispatch is refused.

deepseek.note: METERED — real money. Backend implementation and review. No vision: never send it a screenshot or a task that needs one.

antigravity.note: Very fast. Frontend work. ~16k input-token floor per call. trustFlag --dangerously-skip-permissions approved 2026-08-25 after a headless dispatch returned no work done — agy auto-denies any tool permission it cannot prompt for. It AUTO-APPROVES EVERY TOOL the lane runs, which is a larger grant than directory trust; agy has no smaller flag. Chosen over adding allow-rules to agy's own settings.json so the grant stays here and revoking it is deleting this line.

composer.note: Long multi-file implementation runs. Shares the Cursor allowance with grok. trustFlag --yolo approved 2026-08-25: it auto-approves every command this lane runs, which is what a long unattended build needs. Downgrade to "--trust" for directory trust alone, or delete the key to revoke.

grok.note: Analysis, research, single-shot code. Its agentic coding regressed against 4.5 — do not give it long autonomous runs. Shares the Cursor allowance with composer. No trustFlag: untested here and not approved. If it hits "Workspace Trust Required", ask before adding one — "--trust" is the smaller grant.

codex.note: UNSANDBOXED — danger-full-access, approval never. All-rounder, punches above its size. Highest-risk lane in this file.
